claims.text: The coupled tribo-corrosion degradation of HEAs is governed by a dynamic balance between mechanical removal of a passive oxide and its selective reformation.
The initial HEA forms a thin, protective passive oxide film in a corrosive environment.
Selective oxidation in a multi-element HEA produces compositionally heterogeneous oxide films.
The heterogeneous oxide film mediates the interaction between wear and corrosion.
Sliding stresses intermittently remove sections of the passive oxide layer.
Freshly exposed alloy rapidly oxidizes during intervals between mechanical damage events.
Selective oxidation of Cr, Mn, or other passive elements reforms a protective film after wear damage.
Total degradation depends on whether oxide reformation can keep pace with mechanical oxide removal.
At relatively low wear rates, oxide reformation limits the increase in corrosion relative to static immersion.
Healing of the oxide film mitigates wear loss.
When wear removal exceeds oxide reformation kinetics, both wear and corrosion damage increase significantly.
Increasing passive-element concentration lowers total tribo-corrosion degradation.
Increasing passive-element concentration reduces corrosion and controls wear losses.
The prediction holds when oxide reformation kinetics are appreciable relative to oxide removal rates.
Very high chloride concentrations can dissolve the oxide faster than it reforms and cause the prediction to fail.
Extreme mechanical loads can remove the oxide completely and cause the prediction to fail.
Reducing passive-element concentration is expected to slow oxide reformation and increase both wear and corrosion under tribo-corrosion.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as the same HEA composition under static immersion, but the predicted outcome also invokes a 'composition-matched baseline with lower passive element content,' which cannot be composition-matched if its passive-element concentration differs. The experiment further conflates this no-wear baseline with the separate lower-passive-element alloy comparison.
